On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 4 sold over 5 months against an average of 3.6 listed, about 4.5 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 2 sold. Condos and townhomes: 7 sold over 5 months against an average of 6.4 listed, about 4.6 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was August with 4 sold.
How Scott Creek compares with the rest of its city
Scott Creek against its whole city, October 2026: share of listings and sales, sales ratio and rank.

Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings was 2 in June and 4 in October, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall, and it took 1.5% of the city’s 273 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 3 in June to 7 in October (+133.3%), and it took 1.2% of the city’s 596 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Scott Creek for condos and townhomes in August (a sellers’ best bet).
Scott Creek share of Coquitlam listings and sales by month

In Scott Creek, its share of the houses listed in Coquitlam went from 0.5% in June to 1.1% in October and its share of the condos and townhomes listed went from 0.4% to 0.9%. A share that holds steady while the city moves means the community is following the city; a share that drifts means it is moving differently.

blocks.text: Scott Creek: streets and boundaries

items.t: Scott Creek the neighbourhood is the Lansdowne Drive pocket in northwest Coquitlam, and its defining line is the creek itself, not a City boundary: the City publishes no boundary for this sub-area name, so the creek corridor and the Lansdowne Drive and Falcon Drive streets are the check.
Scott Creek Linear Park, at 2695 Runnel Drive, runs along a portion of Scott Creek on the pocket's west side, and its trails connect neighbourhoods through the creek corridor.

blocks.text: Scott Creek: the housing stock

items.t: The housing around Runnel Drive and Lansdowne Drive faces a linear park, not a commercial strip: Scott Creek Linear Park is a trail park along the creek, so creek-side lots here back onto a public riparian corridor rather than another street.

blocks.text: Scott Creek: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Riparian edges are a protected feature, not landscaping a buyer can clear: the City's Scott Creek Linear Park page explains that the edges of wetlands and waterways are riparian areas, and that restoration projects in the creek improve habitat for coho and chum salmon, cutthroat and steelhead trout.

blocks.text: Scott Creek: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Scott Creek Linear Park's address is 2695 Runnel Drive, a side street off the Lansdowne Drive corridor, not a main-road entrance.
The creek beside these houses is a salmon creek, not a ditch: the City states Scott Creek feeds the Coquitlam River and supports the Lower Coquitlam Watershed.

Hoy Creek Linear Park, south of this pocket in City Centre, is the paired creek park: the City states its trails connect neighbourhoods and that coho and chum salmon are raised at the Hoy Creek Fish Hatchery there.

Salmon viewing for Scott Creek is from public areas beside Guildford Way and off Lansdowne Drive, per the Hoy-Scott watershed reporting — a seasonal creek activity on this pocket's south and west edges.

blocks.text: Scott Creek: costs and taxes

items.t: The neighbourhood-specific cost check is the creek permit: a Runnel Drive or Lansdowne Drive lot within 30 metres of the Scott Creek bank can carry Watercourse Protection Development Permit conditions that an interior lot does not.

blocks.text: Scott Creek: getting around

items.t: Route 186 runs David Avenue at the pocket's north side and route 187 runs Johnson Street at its east side, per their TransLink timetables.

No SkyTrain station is in Scott Creek; the rail connection for routes 185, 186 and 187 is Coquitlam Central Station, south of the pocket, on the Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and the West Coast Express.

blocks.text: Scott Creek: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area layer for any lot backing onto Scott Creek Linear Park: within 30 metres of top of bank or ravine bank in this plan area the permit can set riparian, runoff and slope conditions, and the guide does not set a final lot-level setback.

Check slope and wildfire layers on the City's Schedule B environmental development permit mapping, which maps unstable slopes and the Interface Wildfire Risk Management boundary for the City Centre and Northeast areas; it shows boundaries, not a lot conclusion.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Scott Creek?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 4 houses and 7 condos and townhomes listed in Scott Creek. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Scott Creek from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 4 houses and 7 condos and townhomes sold in Scott Creek over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in June with 2 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in August with 4 sold.

faq.q: How big is Scott Creek compared with the rest of Coquitlam?
faq.a: In October 2026, Scott Creek held 1.1% of the 378 detached houses listed in Coquitlam and 0.9% of the 779 condos and townhomes listed in Coquitlam.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Scott Creek?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 36.4% of the 11 homes listed in Scott Creek and condos and townhomes made up 63.6%; of the 1 that sold, houses were 100.0% and condos and townhomes 0.0%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Scott Creek than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was 2 in June and 4 in October 2026, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall; condos and townhomes rose from 3 in June to 7 in October 2026 (+133.3%).

faq.q: What fish are in Scott Creek itself?
faq.a: Scott Creek supports coho and chum salmon, cutthroat and steelhead trout, according to the City's Scott Creek Linear Park page. The creek is part of the waterway network feeding the Coquitlam River and the Lower Coquitlam Watershed, and ongoing restoration and enhancement projects are improving fish habitat along this Runnel Drive corridor.

faq.q: Is the creek park separate from Eagle Ridge Park?
faq.a: Yes, they are two different City parks serving this pocket. Scott Creek Linear Park, at 2695 Runnel Drive, is the trail corridor along Scott Creek itself.
Catchment is by permanent home address, so run the exact address in the SD43 School Locator.
